must_find.summary: POST /v1/invites returns status 200 instead of the planned 201 (D1 and the /v1 convention).
The response uses the field `expires_at` instead of the planned camelCase `expiresAt` (toJson in src/invites/routes.ts), in both create and list responses.

GET /v1/invites uses offset pagination (`?page=` with `{items, page, total}`) instead of the planned cursor pagination (`?cursor=&limit=` → `{items, nextCursor}`, as in /v1/teams); the store exposes list(offset, limit) instead of listAfter(cursorId, limit).

nice_to_find.summary: The tests assert the deviating contract (status 200, expires_at, page-based listing) instead of the planned one, so they wouldn't catch the contract drift.
InviteStore exposes `list(offset, limit)` rather than the planned `listAfter(cursorId, limit)`.

must_not_flag.summary: The store keeps internal `createdBy`/`createdAt` fields that are not exposed in responses; D1 explicitly allows internal fields as long as they aren't returned.
Reusing the existing `isEmail`/`parseLimit` helpers from src/http/validate.ts is what the plan asked for, not drift.
Requests pass through the pre-existing requestLogger middleware; it is not a new, unplanned change.
